preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(s) <= 2 * 10**5 for s in stdin.split()[1:])
preconditions.description: All elements in S are distinct positive integers within the range [1, 200000].
The first line contains an integer n (1 ≤ n ≤ 200000), and the second line contains exactly n distinct integers.

postconditions.description: The first line of stdout is the largest non-negative integer x such that a magical permutation exists for integers 0 to 2^x - 1. The subsequent lines contain exactly 2^x integers forming a valid magical permutation.

postconditions.expression: all(0 <= int(num) < 2**x for num in permutation) and len(set(permutation)) == 2**x
postconditions.description: The permutation contains all integers from 0 to 2^x - 1 exactly once.

postconditions.expression: all((int(permutation[i]) ^ int(permutation[i+1])) in set(map(int, stdin.split()[1:])) for i in range(len(permutation)-1))
postconditions.description: For every pair of consecutive elements in the permutation, their bitwise XOR is an element of S.

postconditions.expression: x == max(0, max(x_val for x_val in range(0, 21) if exists_magical_permutation(x_val, S)))
postconditions.description: x is the largest non-negative integer for which a magical permutation exists, where S is the set of input integers.
